status: Prospective widening of the v1.4 head-to-head pilot to the six primary datasets, written before scoring the added datasets with OpenJev. The four v1.4 datasets keep their exact selected groups because the selection salt is unchanged. Not external preregistration.
runtime: Original upstream direct.score with CPU-only checkpoint loading adapter; BF16, four torch threads, batch 1, native Transformers, no quantization, no truncation, no decoding. 0.8B is an explicitly substituted capacity control, not the published 4B benchmark.
source: ProEval revision and file hashes in transfer_protocol.json are unchanged from v1.3; v1.5 adds the two datasets whose pinned hashes appear there.
worker_pool: replacement, the four identities fixed in v1.3
selection: First unique groups after sorting by SHA256(openjev-h2h-v1:group); the v1.3 train/dev/test split is retained. Salt unchanged from v1.4 so every previously scored group is still selected and the earlier 128-case result is directly comparable rather than replaced. No selection by errors, disagreement or model confidence.
shared_panel: v1.3 fixed3 panel selected on train/development data. Both empirical_fixed3 and OpenJev receive exactly these same three acquired answers. OpenJev additionally reads task text and receives the same training-derived conditional candidate error estimates. Errors for the current test task are forbidden inputs.
calibration: Regularized logistic success predictor on the development cases of all six datasets (96 in total); C=1, features are candidate log-odds and normalized action entropy. Constant-label development uses Beta(1,1) smoothing. Test labels never update the calibrator. Raw option probability is not claimed to be correctness probability.
uncertainty: 2000 paired question-group bootstraps stratified by dataset and macro averaged; conditional on fixed fit and inference records. Pilot-scale intervals, not a confirmatory SOTA claim.
accounting: Report worker-acquisition objective separately from measured selector CPU wall time and tokens. No invented dollar conversion. Publish a selector-overhead sensitivity grid; actual worker inference latency is unavailable.
verification: Check exact upstream readout hash, checkpoint revision, full loading, matching test IDs, query budget, authorized candidate selection, logits simplex, source hashes and no gold in rendered requests. Repeat repeated_forward_test_groups forward calls and reverse reverse_order_test_groups option sets per dataset per model. These are robustness probes, not independent new tasks. Warmup excluded and counted. Request hashes are compared against this canonical fixture, so a mismatch means the case, panel, split or action contract differs, not that two hosts rounded differently.
limits: Hosted CPU timings cannot be compared with published GPU or service speedups
192 test groups across six existing benchmarks remain a pilot, not global superiority evidence
gqa candidates were produced with image access that the selector never has, so that dataset is not a clean text-only reasoning comparison

Two independent hosted executions of this identical pinned pipeline did not reproduce every selector decision, although every symbolic control row was identical; the paired intervals condition on one recorded execution and exclude that run-to-run component
request_fixture: Candidate error estimates are rounded to 8 decimal places before rendering, so a case serializes to byte-identical request text on every host. Estimates come from a fit, and re-fitting under a different BLAS build moves their last bits; the v1.4 pilot serialized full precision and needed a ULP search to recover 464 recorded request hashes. Rounding is far below any decision-relevant precision and removes the failure mode by construction rather than recovering from it.
